meta.request: Run a risk review of this document

risks.title: Break Notice is irrevocable
risks.summary: Once served, a Break Notice cannot be withdrawn, even if the Landlord's conditions later prove impossible to meet or the Tenant's business position changes. The Tenant is committed to the break before knowing whether it can complete it.
risks.quote: A Break Notice, once given, shall be irrevocable.

risks.title: Break Notice void if any condition fails
risks.summary: If any break condition is not met, the Break Notice is of no effect and the lease continues. There is no cure period or Landlord obligation to warn the Tenant, so a technical failure could leave the Tenant bound for a further term.
risks.quote: If any of the conditions in clause 8.3.1 are not satisfied, the Break Notice shall be of no effect and this Lease shall continue in full force and effect.

risks.title: Break requires vacant possession of whole Premises
risks.summary: Exercising the break requires vacant possession of the whole Premises on the Break Date, free of all occupiers and subtenants. Because subletting of part is prohibited, this is a significant practical hurdle.
risks.quote: the Tenant gives vacant possession of the whole of the Premises to the Landlord on or before the Break Date

risks.title: Six months' rent 'Break Premium' payable as a condition
risks.summary: Exercising the break requires payment of six months' rent on the Break Date, in cleared funds, on top of the vacant possession requirement. This is a substantial cash cost at the 2029 and 2034 break dates and is a condition precedent, not a compensation payment.
risks.quote: a sum equivalent to six (6) months' rent at the rate payable immediately before the Break Date

risks.title: Upward-only rent review
risks.summary: Rent can only increase at the 2029 and 2034 reviews, never decrease, even if the market falls. Combined with the 15-year hypothetical letting term, the Tenant bears the full downside of market movements.
risks.quote: The rent review shall be upward only.

risks.title: Uncapped and unqualified service charge pass-through
risks.summary: All costs of the Landlord's structural, roof, plant and common-area obligations are recoverable through the service charge at a fixed 18.7% share. The lease contains no cap, budget, audit right or exclusion for landlord-default costs.
risks.quote: The cost of the Landlord's obligations under this clause 4.2 shall be recoverable from the Tenant as part of the service charge

risks.title: Insurance excess and premium passed to Tenant
risks.summary: The Tenant reimburses the full insurance premium and any policy excess, with no cap or control over the Landlord's insurance arrangements. The Landlord's subrogation waiver is only a reasonable-endeavours obligation.
risks.quote: of the premium paid or payable by the Landlord for such insurance and any excess applicable under the policy

risks.title: Subrogation waiver only on reasonable endeavours
risks.summary: The Landlord need only use reasonable endeavours to procure a waiver of subrogation against the Tenant. The Tenant could face insurer claims for Insured Risks even where it is not at fault.
risks.quote: The Landlord shall use reasonable endeavours to procure that the insurer waives all rights of subrogation against the Tenant

risks.title: Broad uncapped general indemnity
risks.summary: The Tenant indemnifies the Landlord against all losses arising directly or indirectly from any act or omission of the Tenant, its invitees, any breach of the lease, or the exercise of its rights. There is no cap, no fault threshold and no carve-out for Landlord negligence.
risks.quote: arising directly or indirectly out of: (a) any act, omission or negligence of the Tenant

risks.title: Environmental indemnity extends to statutory liabilities
risks.summary: The Tenant's environmental indemnity expressly covers Part IIA EPA 1990 and Water Resources Act 1991 liabilities and any future environmental legislation, with no time limit or cap. This may extend to contamination the Tenant did not cause, depending on how 'attributable to' is read.
risks.quote: the Tenant's environmental indemnity shall include liability under Part IIA of the Environmental Protection Act 1990

risks.title: Tenant repairs internal structural surfaces
risks.summary: The Tenant must keep internal surfaces of load-bearing walls, columns, floors and window frames in repair and decorated to first-class standard. This pushes some structural-adjacent costs onto the Tenant, though clause 4.3 limits the repair standard to the schedule of condition.
risks.quote: including the internal surfaces of all external and load-bearing walls, floors, ceilings, columns, doors, windows and window frames

risks.title: Absolute prohibition on subletting part
risks.summary: Any subletting of part of the Premises is prohibited outright, with no landlord consent mechanism. This removes flexibility to reduce space during the term and may reduce the lease's marketability.
risks.quote: The Tenant shall not sublet any part of the Premises (as distinct from the whole).

risks.title: Whole subletting at not less than open market rent
risks.summary: Any subletting of the whole must be at a rent no lower than the higher of the passing rent and open market rent. This restricts the Tenant's ability to sublet at a discount in a weak market.
risks.quote: any subletting shall be at a rent not less than the higher of the rent payable under this Lease

risks.title: Schedules and plans referenced but not provided
risks.summary: The lease refers to Schedules 1 to 4 and to plans, including the service charge provisions (Schedule 3) and the schedule of condition (Schedule 4). None are included in the document, so the rights granted, service charge mechanics and condition baseline cannot be verified.
risks.quote: annexed to this Lease at Schedule 4

risks.title: No guarantor or security for the Tenant covenant
risks.summary: The Tenant is an LLP executing by two members, with no guarantee, rent deposit or other security in the document. The 15-year covenant depends entirely on the LLP's financial strength, which is not verified here.
risks.quote: acting by two members:

risks.title: Permitted Use definition is internally inconsistent
risks.summary: Clause 1.1 defines the Permitted Use by reference to Class E(g)(i), but clause 6.1 adds a description of business operations 'carried out in a residential area', which is the older wording and may create interpretive ambiguity.
risks.quote: being offices for the conduct of business operations that may be carried out in a residential area without detriment to its amenity

risks.title: Landlord may add Insured Risks unilaterally
risks.summary: The definition of Insured Risks lets the Landlord add risks it 'reasonably determines', which may increase premiums passed through to the Tenant under clause 5.3.
risks.quote: such other risks as the Landlord may from time to time reasonably determine

The risk review is complete. The table lists 17 risks: 8 high, 7 medium and 2 low.

The headline findings are:

- **Break clause (cl. 8):** This is the most significant issue. The break at 2029 and 2034 is conditional on vacant possession of the whole Premises, payment of six months' rent, and no unremedied breach. The Break Notice is irrevocable, and if any condition fails, the notice is void and the lease continues. The Tenant could be locked in for a further term after serving notice.
- **Rent review (cl. 3.2):** The review is upward only, so rent cannot fall at the 2029 or 2034 reviews even if the market does.
- **Service charge and indemnities (cl. 4.2.3, 5.3, 9):** The Landlord's structural and plant costs are passed to the Tenant (18.7% share) without a cap, and the general and environmental indemnities are broad and uncapped.
- **Missing schedules:** Schedules 1 to 4 and the plans are referred to but not included in the document, so the service charge mechanics and the schedule of condition cannot be verified.

commercial-lease-100-bishopsgate.pdf.final_text:
The risk review has identified 13 material risks: 6 high, 5 medium and 2 low.

**Headline findings:**

- **Break clause (high):** The break is conditional on 12 months' irrevocable notice, full vacant possession, and payment of a six-month rent Break Premium. If any condition fails, the notice is void, so the tenant could lose the break entirely.
- **Upward-only rent review (high):** Clause 3.2.5 provides that rent cannot fall at the 2029 or 2034 reviews, and there is no cap or collar.
- **Environmental and general indemnities (high):** Clauses 9.1 and 9.2 are uncapped, the environmental indemnity expressly extends to future legislation, and the general indemnity covers losses "directly or indirectly" arising from the tenant's rights, with no carve-out for landlord negligence.
- **Missing schedules (high):** Schedules 1 to 4 are referred to but not included, including the service charge provisions (Schedule 3) and the schedule of condition (Schedule 4). The service charge and repair baseline cannot be properly assessed until these are provided.

The medium-rated points concern the full landlord-cost service charge pass-through, the tenant's "every part" repairing covenant, open-ended Insured Risks, and restrictions on subletting. The low-rated points are the rent review and arbitration overlap and residual Class B1 wording in the permitted use clause.

The document also has blank signature blocks, so it may be an unexecuted copy. I did not identify a guarantor or rent deposit, which may be worth confirming given the tenant is an LLP.

The risk review found nine material risks: two high, five medium and two low. The table above sets them out with supporting quotes.

**Headline findings:**

- **Height covenant (high):** The 1952 covenant caps buildings at four storeys, measured from 1952 ground level. The consented scheme includes a four-storey block, so a dispute over measurement could put it at risk of enforcement.
- **Section 106 obligations (high):** The registered agreement requires 17 affordable units, £185,000 for highways and £75,000 for open space, plus a local employment commitment. These need to be priced into the appraisal.
- **Sewer easement (medium):** A shared sewer crosses the site, with access rights for the statutory undertaker and adjoining owners. This may constrain the layout of the residential blocks.

The report is also not an official copy and cannot be relied on under s.67 LRA 2002, so official copies and the title plan should be obtained before any reliance.
